battery.chemistry.notes: Estimated: GUESS: Wikipedia says lithium-ion by Deutsche Accumotive (the 2017 car "LG chemistry, 96 cells"); LG Chem cells are NMC but no page says so. Owner decision.

ac_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Wikipedia states 3.3 kW for the ED2 car; the EPA 240 V charge time (6 h for the 2013 car, vs 3 h in 2017 with 7.2 kW) is consistent with the same charger on the ED3. German Wikipedia says 3.7 kW for the EU ED3 and Fleetnews (per the fact-checker) 3 kW; no North American page for 2013-16.

battery.nominal_voltage_class.notes: Estimated: GUESS: no page states the pack voltage; the 2017 pack has 96 cells in series (Wikipedia), about 350 V nominal, and the ED2/ED3 packs are assumed the same class. Owner decision.

battery.preconditioning.notes: Estimated: Green Cars Compare: no DC fast charging, and no battery-warming feature is described for the smart ED on any page opened.

dc_max_kw.notes: Estimated: Green Cars Compare (ED2 page): "does not support DC fast charging"; other years assumed the same (EPA lists only 240 V charge times; the 2012 optional quick-charge announcement was for Europe).

charge_port.notes: Estimated: AC-only car in the US/Canada (no DC port); J1772 is the North American AC inlet.

supercharger_access.notes: Estimated: no DC port, so no Supercharger access.
